text:
Jason Dickinson is the checking center Edmonton's stars aren't supposed to have to think about, and the results have mostly let them. He has 4 points in 12 games, including a goal against Vancouver on Nov 7, and the Oilers have won most of the nights he's dressed.

Underneath, the picture is shakier. At five on five Edmonton has had just 29.9% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 20 points worse than without him, yet the Oilers have scored 4.89 more goals than those chances deserved while he's out there. A gap like that rarely holds, in either direction. Part of the explanation is his job. In his last season in Chicago, Evolving-Hockey had him facing the other team's best (98th percentile competition) with weak teammates, and still taking chances away, in the 86th percentile among forwards. Twelve games is a small sample for a defensive center, and the hard matchups will push his numbers down. But if the chance share doesn't improve, the good bounces won't keep covering for it, and that's the thing to watch.
headline: Jason Dickinson's results are outrunning his chances
